output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in the new documentation suite, not to the fungicide, Meridane's equipment, the route, or Lower Serra growers. The mandarin product record was copied from an avocado record on 1 Aug, and its 7.0°C carriage temperature was never changed. The specification is 4.0°C. Every Tallis-booked Meridane container ran at 7°C and was rejected, with decay of 9–14%. Meridane's units held that setpoint, as its letter said. The earlier Meridane container (K1) was booked by email at 4°C, so it passed despite the 26-day transit. All Coastway containers at 4°C passed, including those packed with the new fungicide. K3 used old fungicide and still failed. Lower Serra fruit did decay more within rejected containers. That is not shown to be a cause, because accepted containers were not surveyed. I'm quite sure of the main finding. Next steps: correct the product record to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a pre-submission check of reefer settings against the specification. Do not file the cargo claim, suspend Lower Serra, or revert the fungicide. Warn the importer.
